newsitem.title: UK: Courtaulds extends loss after results.
newsitem.headline: Courtaulds extends loss after results.

text.p: Shares in Courtaulds Plc dropped to a six-month low on Tuesday amid continued reaction to the chemical company's first-half results last week and fears it will lose its position in the blue-chip FTSE 100 index.
The FTSE committee meets next Wednesday to review membership of the index. Courtaulds' position is at risk because its market value is among the lowest of the index's current members.

The stock was down 11p at 405-1/2 by 1014 GMT in active trade of 3.9 million shares, after touching a low of 403 -- the lowest since May and extending a fall from its year's high of 490p set October 3.
"We saw a few sellers around last night and there were some more around this morning," said a market-maker in the stock at one leading brokerage.

Courtaulds last week posted a 5.6 percent decline in first-half pre-tax profit to 64 million stg, but was guardedly optimistic on prospects for the second half of the year. Analysts pointed out that earnings expectations for Courtaulds had already been lowered in the run-up to the results and that expectations of a recovery in the company's profits had been deferred.

"It is just out of favour at the moment," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "Everyone has been forecasting a strong recovery in profits but the problem is that it seems to be coming tomorrow rather than today."
"Eventually it will start firing on all cylinders but at the moment it is a bit unloved, that is the reality."
